ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Jeffrey fires three arrows at each of four archery targets. He scores 29 points on the first target, 43 on the second and 47 on the third. How many points does Jeffrey score on the fourth target?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Looking at the four targets from left to right, each target has three arrows. The 1st target has 1 arrow in the outer ring and 2 arrows in the middle ring; the 2nd target has 2 arrows in the center and 1 arrow in the outer ring; the 3rd target has 2 arrows in the center and 1 arrow in the middle ring; the 4th target has 1 arrow in the center, 1 arrow in the middle ring, and 1 arrow in the outer ring. Reasoning: Let the score of the outer ring be O, the score of the middle ring be M, and the score of the center be C. According to the total scores of the first three targets: the 1st target gives O + 2M = 29; the 2nd target gives 2C + O = 43; the 3rd target gives 2C + M = 47. Subtract the second equation from the third equation to obtain M - O = 4, so M = O + 4. Substitute into O + 2M = 29 to obtain O + 2(O + 4) = 29, namely 3O + 8 = 29, so O = 7, M = 11. Then from 2C + O = 43 we get 2C + 7 = 43, so C = 18. The total score of the 4th target is C + M + O = 18 + 11 + 7 = 36.

method.method_draft: Read the four targets from left to right. From the image, classify each of the three arrows by scoring region: target 1 has 1 arrow in the outer ring and 2 in the middle ring; target 2 has 2 arrows in the center and 1 in the outer ring; target 3 has 2 arrows in the center and 1 in the middle ring; target 4 has 1 arrow in each of the center, middle ring, and outer ring. From the text, use the totals for the first three targets: 29, 43, and 47. Let outer = O, middle = M, center = C. Set up equations O + 2M = 29, 2C + O = 43, and 2C + M = 47. Subtract the second equation from the third to get M - O = 4, combine with O + 2M = 29 to get M = 11 and O = 7, then find C = 18. For the fourth target, add C + M + O = 18 + 11 + 7 = 36.
